name: Using 3D ADU Renderings to Improve Design Decisions

mainEntity.name: How do I evaluate 3D renderings and virtual walkthroughs from an ADU design contractor to avoid costly design mistakes?
mainEntity.text: How do I evaluate 3D renderings and virtual walkthroughs from an ADU design contractor to avoid costly design mistakes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many Los Angeles ADU design contractors now include 3D renderings or virtual walkthroughs, but homeowners often treat them as pretty images instead of decision tools. To avoid expensive design mistakes, insist that the 3D model include standard-sized furniture, appliances, and plumbing fixtures, not just empty rooms. As you review, focus on functional questions: Can two people cook comfortably in the kitchen at once? Is there enough clearance around the bed and dining area? Do door swings conflict with furniture or each other? Examine window placement relative to neighbors to balance natural light with privacy; ask for views from inside looking out, not just exterior perspectives. Consider where you will store everyday items like vacuum cleaners, luggage, and pantry staples, and whether closets and built-ins are sufficient. Request both daytime and nighttime lighting simulations so you can judge natural light and artificial lighting layers. Finally, simulate daily routines: entering with groceries, guests using the bathroom, or an elderly occupant navigating at night. Encourage your designer to adjust the layout now based on these observations, because changes are far cheaper at the rendering stage than after permit approval or during construction, when even minor revisions can trigger delays and change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use 3D renderings and walkthroughs to check furniture layout, door swings, window placement, light, privacy, and storage. Ask your ADU design contractor to show realistic scale with standard furniture, then walk through day-to-night scenarios and guest circulation to catch awkward layouts before finalizing plans.
